 10 Things To Know – Auburn 
 Hunter Corneliusen 
 November 6, 2026 
 With four games remaining in the regular season, the Hogs head to the Plains for their penultimate SEC road contest of the year. Kickoff between Arkansas and Auburn from inside Jordan-Hare Stadium is scheduled for 11:45 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 7, on SEC Network.
 1 – LB Ja’Quavion Smith leads the Hogs with 53 tackles this season while collecting 3.5 tackles for loss in addition to a sack. The Howard transfer ranks third among all active Razorbacks in career tackles for loss during his collegiate career with 17.5
 2 –Arkansas has forced a turnover in three consecutive games this season, its longest such streak in a season since forcing a turnover in four consecutive games from Oct. 21-Nov. 18, 2023.
 3 – Saturday’s matchup will be the 36th meeting between the programs, with Auburn leading the all-time series 21-13-1.  The Tigers took the last matchup between the teams, 33-24 on Oct. 25, 2025, in Fayetteville. Arkansas won the last meeting at Auburn, 24-14 on Sept. 21, 2024.
 4 – LB Bradley Shaw led Arkansas and tied a career high with nine tackles in addition to two pass breakups and a fumble recovery against Missouri. It marked the second consecutive season Shaw had recovered a fumble against Missouri and the first time a Razorback has recovered a fumble in consecutive seasons against the same opponent since at least 1995.
 5 – Arkansas has scored in 66 consecutive games, tied for the fourth-longest streak in program history, and most since a 66-game streak from Nov. 2, 2013 to Nov. 17, 2018. Arkansas was last shut out on Oct. 2, 2021, in a loss to No. 2 Georgia.
 6 – WR Antonio Jordan has led Arkansas in receiving in consecutive games. Last week against Missouri, the Warren, Ark., product hauled in a career-high seven receptions for 106 yards, recording his first career 100-yard receiving game. In a 31-21 win at Vanderbilt on Oct. 17, Jordan led the Hogs with five receptions for 74 yards.
 7 – As American Conference foes, Ryan Silverfield (Memphis’ head coach from 2020-25) owned a perfect 3-0 head-to-head record against Alex Golesh (South Florida’s head coach from 2023-25).
 8 – The Razorbacks’ 244 consecutive extra-points made streak, which began on Dec. 5, 2020, is the longest streak nationally by date.
 9 – With seven catches for 106 yards the last time out against Missouri, WR Antonio Jordan became the first Arkansas player to have a 100+ yard receiving game in their first collegiate start since Jonathan Williams (3 receptions, 150 yards) accomplished the feat in a 49-7 win over Kentucky on Oct. 13, 2012.
 10 – The Razorback defense has recorded 10 turnovers (5 INT + 5 FR) through eight games this season. Arkansas tallied just nine turnovers (6 INT + 3 FR) in 12 games during the 2025 campaign.
